title: Find the Number of Copy Arrays
summary: Given an array original of length n and a 2D array bounds of size n x 2, where bounds[i] = [ui, vi], find the count of arrays copy of length n that satisfy: 1.
statement: Given an array original of length n and a 2D array bounds of size n x 2, where bounds[i] = [ui, vi], find the count of arrays copy of length n that satisfy: 1. (copy[i] - copy[i - 1]) equals (original[i] - original[i - 1]) for 1 <= i <= n - 1. 2. ui <= copy[i] <= vi for 0 <= i <= n - 1. Return the total count of such arrays.
constraints: original and bounds have equal nonzero length; each bound is an inclusive [low,high] interval.
Every adjacent difference in copy must equal the corresponding difference in original.
Count integer copy arrays satisfying every positional bound.
hints: Equal adjacent differences force every copy value to equal original[i] plus one shared integer shift.
Translate each positional bound into an allowed shift interval and intersect them all.
Update the maximum lower shift and minimum upper shift; return the inclusive intersection size or zero.
A chosen first value fixes the shared shift and therefore the entire copy, giving a one-to-one correspondence with feasible shifts.

tests.explanation: The valid common shifts are zero and one, producing two arrays.
No common shift can place both values at zero while preserving their difference, so return zero.
